mintAuthority.summary: GHO has economically unbounded native issuance authority: the DAO executor can add arbitrary EOA facilitators without a collateral check, and the independent 2-of-3 Risk Council can raise the mainnet direct facilitator bucket and mint to any recipient without a deposit. Current buckets are numeric limits, not economic backing constraints. Governance V3 uses past-block storage proofs and a delayed ordinary execution path, but the Council path prevents governance-only qualification; no active mint compromise is alleged.

controls.label: GHO Bucket Steward
controls.capDescription: Holds GHO BUCKET_MANAGER_ROLE. The verified steward permits only Risk Council increases for controlled facilitators, with each increase no greater than the current capacity and a one-day debounce between updates. The DAO executor controls the approved facilitator list. The debounce is not an execution timelock.

governedIssuance.votingPowerEvidence: GovernanceCore.activateVoting snapshots blockhash(block.number - 1), stores proposal.snapshotBlockHash and forwards that hash to the selected VotingMachine. VotingMachineWithProofs validates voting-asset storage proofs against the proposal block hash before VotingStrategy.getVotingPower; balances and delegations are historical Ethereum snapshot state, not transaction-live balances. This voting-power condition is met, but the independently authorized Risk Council mint path and incomplete execution closure make this governed attempt ineligible.

review.evidence: At Ethereum block 26095800 (2026-10-01), canonical GHO bytecode matched the verified GhoToken deployment and its EIP-1967 implementation and correct admin slots were zero. The ACL Admin executor retained DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, FACILITATOR_MANAGER_ROLE, and BUCKET_MANAGER_ROLE. getFacilitatorsList() returned eight registered facilitators and totalSupply() returned 699,000,000 GHO; the Arbitrum and Monad GSM facilitators each had 50,000,000 GHO capacity and level. The token's verified mint function enforces each facilitator's bucket capacity, while DAO-authorized administration can add facilitators or raise capacities. The separately verified GHO Bucket Steward also holds BUCKET_MANAGER_ROLE and can increase approved native facilitator capacities under its own Risk Council and debounce checks. Contract-governed issuance has no off-chain reserve reconciliation requirement; no prudential supervision of this native mint boundary is evidenced in the reviewed protocol disclosures. D14/D29 review on 2026-10-03 reuses the successful executor addFacilitator(0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dead,"parity",uint128.max) simulation at Ethereum block 26112822 (hash 0x9a43012d71f59ade74c58a438ae4cf7eba960288f5357ddd8203d3a0ac51042a). GhoToken.mint checks facilitator bucket capacity/level, not collateral or code identity, so the economic cap is unbounded. At the same pin, getFacilitatorsList and every getFacilitatorBucket confirm all eight existing capacities/levels. Bucket Steward.getControlledFacilitators returns Core 0x5513224daaeabca31af5280727878d52097afa05, Horizon 0xe10c78a3ac7f016ed2de1a89c5479b1039eab9ea, mainnet GSMs 0xe9ac5231faecb633da0fe85fcb2785b8363427d2 and Lido 0x2ce01c87fec1b71a9041c52caed46fc5f4807285. Pinned EIP-1967 slots and exact source/runtime matches bind the three pool minters to their verified GhoDirectMinter implementations; mintAndSupply mints first and deposits the newly minted GHO into the pool, rather than checking a new borrower collateral deposit at this boundary. Their owner is the executor and guardian is the Risk Council. Critically, mainnet GSMs is verified GhoDirectFacilitator, not a deposit-checking GSM contract: mint(account,amount) checks only MINTER_ROLE. Full grant/revoke history plus hasRole reads identify both executor and Risk Council as live MINTER_ROLE holders there. Council is a 2/3 Safe; its pinned eth_call raising that bucket from 310M to 311M succeeds immediately. Thus Council can increase capacity and cause durable arbitrary-recipient issuance without collateral, defeating the delegated-collateral-only and governor-only gates. Its one-day debounce limits repeat updates, not the unavoidable delay before an eligible new update; the Council issuance path minimum is 0 seconds. Ordinary Level-1 governance at this pin has coolDownBeforeVotingStart=86400, votingDuration=259200, COOLDOWN_PERIOD=0 and payload delay=86400. Sequential activation (>86400), queueing (>259200 after activation) and payload execution (>86400 after its queue) impose an integer-timestamp lower bound of 432003 seconds; the zero core cooldown adds nothing, and no overlapping clocks are summed. Cross-chain transport may add latency but is not a certified lower-bound component. Past-block storage-proof voting and facilitator/capacity enumeration are evidenced, yet all authored scopes remain partial because global infrastructure, mutable permission/upgrade/bypass and downstream liability closure are not certified; Council is explicitly independent, not governor-rooted. The curated fallback is unbounded-unreconciled: reconciliation remains not-applicable and supervision none. No active mint incident is evidenced.
